Commute to central Stockholm

From each area's main centre or station to T-Centralen. Public transport: fastest SL trip arriving by 08:00 on a weekday (Tue 10 Nov 2026), walking included. Car: fastest road route without traffic; rush hour is typically slower. Bike: regular bike at about 15 km/h on cycle-friendly roads; an e-bike is roughly a third faster.

Sources: boundaries from SCB (RegSO 2025) and municipal borders from OpenStreetMap-derived open data (okfse/sweden-geojson). Routing: OSRM (car), FOSSGIS routing.openstreetmap.de (bike), SL journey planner via Trafiklab (public transport). Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. Schools: Skolverket (SALSA, average merit value and share eligible for upper secondary, latest year).

All areas ranked

Match score: each priority is scored 0–100 across the 25 areas and weighted by how much it matters to you. Areas over budget or over your max commute are pushed down, not hidden. Prices are average bostadsrätt kr/kvm (villa prices are usually lower per m² outside the inner city). School results are averages for schools located in the area; Swedish school choice means children can attend schools elsewhere.

Neighbourhood guide

25 areas: Stockholm's 12 Mäklarstatistik districts and 13 surrounding municipalities. Click an area for the full profile.

Sources: population, households, housing, tenure, building age and education from SCB (Statistics Sweden), 2025, summed from RegSO small areas for Stockholm's districts and municipality totals for the others. Income: SCB, median disposable income for ages 20–64, 2023 (population-weighted across small areas). Elections: Valmyndigheten, final results of the Riksdag election 13 Sep 2026, with change from 2022; for Stockholm's districts, polling districts are grouped by parish, the same parishes Mäklarstatistik's districts are built from. Prices: Svensk Mäklarstatistik, bostadsrätter. The written overviews are summaries by Claude based on these figures and general knowledge about the areas; they are not official descriptions.

Neighbourhood table

Click a column to sort. Changes use 3-month smoothed kr/kvm.

Items

Sentiment runs from −1 (very negative for the area) to +1 (very positive). Edit a score to correct it; your edits are kept when re-scoring with the word list.

Cross-correlation by lag

Positive lag = the signal comes before the price change. Negative lag = prices move first (e.g. rising prices attracting positive coverage). Dashed lines: approx. 95% band, adjusted for overlapping windows. With “compare areas” on, both the signal and the price change are measured relative to the average of all areas that month.

Scatter at lag months

Each dot is one area-month (signal and price change each standardised within its area).

Between areas: overall coverage vs price growth

One dot per area. Horizontal: average news tone (share of positive minus share of negative articles) over the whole price period. Vertical: total price change over the same period. This shows association between places, not timing — it can't tell whether coverage drives prices, prices drive coverage, or both follow something else (income, schools, crime).

By neighbourhood

Correlation per area at selected lags. Few news items per area make single-area values noisy — trust the pooled row more.

Forecast

Median path with 10–90% range from 400 simulated paths. Model: pooled ridge regression on price momentum, city-wide momentum, policy-rate changes and lagged news, police and planning signals.

Backtest: does news improve the forecast?

Model trained on everything before the held-out months, then asked to predict each of those months one step ahead.

What drives the model

Standardised coefficients: effect on next month's price change (percentage points) of a one-standard-deviation move in each input.

All neighbourhoods

Forecast change over the horizon, with 10–90% range.

This is a statistical model, not financial advice. It extrapolates relationships seen in past data; it cannot foresee shocks such as rule changes or a sudden rate move, and wide ranges are honest about that.

About Stockholm Property Signals

Find your place in Stockholm.

Why this exists

Choosing where to live in Stockholm usually means piecing things together from estate agents' listings, price sites, school rankings, the SL app and word of mouth. Stockholm Property Signals brings it all into one place: what homes cost and how prices are moving, how long the commute is, how good the schools are, who lives in each area and what is happening there. You can compare all 25 areas on equal terms before you book a single viewing.

It is also a research tool. It asks whether local news (good or bad), police incidents and planning decisions show up in house prices, and whether that helps forecast where prices go next. So far the honest answer is that news reflects an area more than it predicts price moves — see the Correlation and Forecast tabs.

What's inside

Map & commute — all areas on one map, with travel times to T-Centralen by public transport, car and bike.
Where should I live? — tell it your budget, household and priorities and get a ranked shortlist with reasons.
Neighbourhoods — a profile of each area: character, who it suits, housing, people, schools, politics and news.
Prices, News, Correlation, Forecast — the market data and the analysis behind it.

How the areas are defined

Stockholm city is split into the 12 districts used by Svensk Mäklarstatistik, which follow the city's old parish boundaries (for example, Gamla stan belongs to Vasastan-Norrmalm and Blackeberg to Bromma-Västerled). The 13 surrounding municipalities are shown as whole municipalities. Statistics for Stockholm's districts are built up from SCB's 127 small areas (RegSO), and election results from the city's polling districts.

Good to know

This is an independent analysis tool, not financial or investment advice. Forecasts are statistical estimates with wide uncertainty. Area averages hide big differences between streets. The written neighbourhood overviews are summaries generated by Claude (Anthropic's AI) from the data and general knowledge, not official descriptions. Prices are average bostadsrätt (apartment) prices per m²; villa prices are not yet included.

Built with Claude. Code and data files: github.com/danielengerby1/stockholm-property-signals

Where the data comes from

All built-in data comes from free, public sources. Collected 3 November 2026.

DataSourceCoverage
Apartment prices (kr/kvm, number sold)Svensk MäklarstatistikMonthly Oct 2022 – Sep 2026; annual from 1996/2005. Källa: Svensk Mäklarstatistik AB.

Population, age, households, house type, tenure, building age, educationSCB – Statistics Sweden2025; small areas (RegSO) and municipalities

Election resultsValmyndighetenRiksdag election 13 Sep 2026 (final), change since 2022
School resultsSkolverketYear-9 merit value, share eligible for upper secondary (SALSA), 738 schools

Map boundariesSCB (RegSO 2025); okfse/sweden-geojsonMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors

Where to get the data

This page can't fetch websites itself, so you download from these sources and drop the files above.

DataSourceHow
Prices per neighbourhoodSvensk MäklarstatistikMonthly kr/kvm for bostadsrätter by Stockholm area. Copy the figures into the price template below.
Individual salesBooli slutpriser, Hemnet såldaExport or copy sold listings with date, price, living area and area name. The importer computes kr/kvm and monthly medians.
National price indexSCB Statistikdatabasen, Valueguard HOXUse as a city-wide baseline (import as area "Stockholm").
News per areaGoogle News RSSOpen a feed for an area, save the page (Ctrl/Cmd+S) and drop it here with that area selected.
Police incidentspolisen.se/api/eventsFree open API, latest ~500 events. Save the JSON and drop it here; events are matched to areas by place names in the text. Import regularly to build up history.
Planning & infrastructureStockholm växer, Region Stockholm (tunnelbana)Add project milestones as news rows with category planning.
Policy rate, mortgage ratesRiksbanken, SCB (KPIF, unemployment)Monthly values in the macro template.
